summary: For children aged 5–7 learning that dinosaurs were real animals that lived an enormously long time ago and that the non-bird dinosaurs (such as T. rex) are now extinct. Two load-bearing ideas: (1) dinosaurs were REAL, known from real bones/fossils, unlike made-up creatures such as dragons; (2) non-bird dinosaurs are EXTINCT (none left alive anywhere) and died out long before any people existed, so people and non-bird dinosaurs never lived together (birds are the one dinosaur group still alive). Use relative time language ('before grandparents, before any people, a very very long time ago') rather than abstract millions of years. The preferred route lets children discover the coexistence myth by placing time markers themselves; alternatives (a museum scene, a few picture questions, a palaeontologist character) are retained for different purposes.
misconceptions: 'Dinosaurs and people (cavemen) lived at the same time' — dinosaurs died out long before any humans existed.
'Dinosaurs are made up, like dragons' — dinosaurs were real animals known from real fossils.
'Some dinosaurs are still alive today' (confusing them with living reptiles like crocodiles or lizards) — non-bird dinosaurs are all extinct.
'Extinct means asleep / hiding / will come back' — extinct means none are left alive anywhere.
'All dinosaurs lived at the same time' — different dinosaurs lived in different ages (introduced more fully later).

activities.title: Time ribbon: place the markers and find the gap
steps: Take a simple long time ribbon/strip and a handful of markers: 'dinosaurs', 'the first people', 'grandparents', 'now'.
Place each marker where you think it belongs along the ribbon.
If you put 'people' next to 'dinosaurs', watch as the grown-up (or the app) stretches the ribbon to open up a huge empty gap, moving 'people' far away from 'dinosaurs'.
Say out loud what the gap shows: the big dinosaurs like T. rex were gone long, long before any people were born.
activities.insight: Non-bird dinosaurs (like T. rex) lived an enormously long time ago and died out long before any people existed — people and these dinosaurs never lived at the same time (busting the cartoon 'cave people + dinosaurs' myth).

activities.title: Two sorters: alive-today vs only-fossils, and real vs pretend
steps: Sort animals into 'alive today' or 'only known from fossils': crocodile, elephant, chicken, T. rex. (The crocodile, elephant and chicken stay in 'alive today'; T. rex moves to 'only fossils'.)
Sort pictures into 'real' or 'pretend': a dinosaur vs a dragon.
When you tap/choose the dinosaur, look at the photo of its actual museum bones that appears; the dragon gets a 'made-up' tag.
Say why a dinosaur is 'real' and a dragon is 'pretend'.
activities.insight: Dinosaurs were real animals known from real bones/fossils, unlike made-up creatures; 'extinct' means none are left alive anywhere, as with T. rex and the other non-bird dinosaurs, and this connects to sorting things that are alive, dead, or never alive.

activities.title: Museum-hall scene: bones, time signpost, and 'is it alive today?'
steps: Explore a scene with a dinosaur skeleton and a present-day street.
Tap/look at the skeleton to reveal 'real bones, real animal'.
Tap/look at a 'time signpost' to reveal 'lived long before people'.
Lift a flap on 'is it alive today?' to reveal 'no — extinct'.
activities.insight: Dinosaurs were real (here are the bones), lived long ago, and are extinct.

activities.title: Talk it through: diagnostic and deeper probes
steps: Respond to a friend's claim: 'Dinosaurs are just pretend, like dragons and unicorns — and anyway, cave people used to keep them as pets.' Is your friend right or wrong?
Explain how we can be so sure dinosaurs were real.
Say whether people ever lived at the same time as dinosaurs.

Answer the deeper questions: How do we know dinosaurs were real if nobody ever saw one alive? Was 'a long time ago' like when grandparents were little, or much, much longer? What does 'extinct' mean, and can you name another extinct animal?
activities.insight: A full understanding holds all three: dinosaurs were real (evidence = fossils); non-bird dinosaurs like T. rex are extinct (none left alive anywhere); and they lived long before any people.

checkQuestion: Your friend says 'Dinosaurs are just pretend, like dragons and unicorns — and anyway, cave people used to keep them as pets.' Is your friend right or wrong? Explain how we can be so sure dinosaurs were real, and whether people ever lived at the same time as them.
checkAnswer: Wrong on both counts. Dinosaurs were real animals, not made up like dragons — we know because we find their fossils: real bones, teeth and footprints turned to rock. And no people lived at the same time as (non-bird) dinosaurs; the dinosaurs died out (went extinct) millions of years ago, long before there were any people. Extinct means none are left alive anywhere.
